methodology: Labeled by Claude reading resume text directly against each JD's stated requirements, blind to the corpus's underlying generation parameters, ranked within tier (not across tiers) per JD. This is an LLM-labeled ground truth, not a human/non-recruiter labeler as originally planned - a real circularity (an LLM judging the data used to grade an LLM scorer), disclosed as a known limitation in eval/results.md and README.md, not glossed over.

rankings.notes: Junior: 001 best-matches core stack (Go/Python, Docker, PostgreSQL, AWS, unit testing) in a single stable role; 002 has REST API/CI/CD/AWS/unit testing but no Python/Go/Docker/PostgreSQL and 3 jobs in 1.2yrs; 003 has fewest matches. Mid: 004 vs 006 is a close call - 006 covers more of the literal requirements (Python, Docker, CI/CD) but has 6 jobs in 6.8yrs with no title progression, while 004 has fewer requirement matches but strong stability, progression, and quantified impact; stability/progression tipped it to 004. Senior: both candidates oddly carry a B.S. Nursing degree (generator artifact, no differentiation); ranked on skill match and stability (007's 3 roles/10yrs vs 008's 6 roles/11yrs).

Junior: 002 and 003 both cover React + a backend language + 2 of the JD's bonus items; 003 edges ahead on employment stability (1 stable role vs 002's 3 roles in 1.2yrs) - close call. Mid: 005 is the only mid candidate with React, the JD's headline requirement, so it wins outright despite a thinner skill list. Senior: neither has React (a real gap for both); ranked on stability as in swe_backend.

None of the three junior candidates list SQL, so ranking rests on Tableau/Power BI + data-pipeline coverage and bonus breadth (009 and 011 both close, 010 weakest on core reqs). Mid: 012 is the only mid candidate with SQL, a 'strong requirement' in the JD, so it wins clearly; 013 vs 014 close call resolved in 013's favor for quantified achievements and stability over 014's flat/qualitative bullets and 6 jobs in 6.8yrs.

Senior: neither 015 nor 016 lists A/B testing (the JD's headline requirement), a real gap for both; broke the tie in 016's favor since it explicitly lists 'dashboarding', a stated bonus item, while 015 does not - a close, arguable call.

Junior: 019 matches all four core requirements (user research, roadmapping, stakeholder management, SQL) outright. Mid: 020 is the most stable tenure-wise (2 roles/6.1yrs) but matches only roadmapping of the four core requirements, so it ranks last despite the stability edge - skill match against stated requirements was weighted more heavily. Senior: 024 has by far the stronger career trajectory (APM->PM->Senior PM, longest tenures) but its skills list barely touches the JD's core requirements, so 023 wins on requirement match.

None of the junior/mid candidates list A/B testing, the JD's headline skill; rankings lean on the SQL match plus overall analytical depth. Senior 023 vs 024 is a genuine close call - both match A/B testing and Figma equally, neither has SQL; resolved in 024's favor on overall career trajectory (12.2yrs, clear APM->PM->Sr.PM progression, longest average tenure).

Junior 026 has the strongest skill match (CRM + consultative selling + forecasting) but a severe red flag of 3 jobs in 0.5 years - ranked first anyway on requirement match, but this is a close/arguable call given the stability concern. Mid: 029 vs 030 close call - 030 is far more stable (2 roles/5.6yrs vs 029's 6 roles/6.1yrs) but 029 covers more of the JD's bonus list (forecasting + account management vs just account management); resolved in 029's favor on skill breadth.
Junior 025 and 026 match the same core+bonus skills (cold outreach, CRM, negotiation); 025 wins on stability (1 stable role vs 026's 3 jobs in 0.5yrs).

Core requirements (patient assessment, care planning, BLS, EHR/Epic) were weighted above bonus items (ACLS, wound care, charge nurse) throughout. Senior: both 039 and 040 carry a Charge Nurse title (satisfying the charge-nurse bonus), but 039 matches 3 of 4 core requirements versus 040 matching none explicitly, so 039 wins clearly despite similar tenure and experience length.
